The hosted MORIE services, as the project site currently describes them

Source: R/services.R
svcs.Rd

Reads https://rmorie.com/.well-known/morie-services.json, a signed document naming the curated-data service and its sign-in: their endpoints, whether each is "key" (reachable with a key requested on the site) or "off", and a notice. The signature (ML-DSA-44, public key pinned in this package) is checked before anything in it is believed, so the endpoints can move or be switched off on the site without a package release, and a document that does not verify is ignored. The result is cached for a day; without a network the cached copy is used, then the copy bundled with the package.

Usage

svcs(refresh = FALSE, maxage = 86400, tmout = 20, offline = FALSE)

Arguments

refresh

Logical scalar, default FALSE: TRUE fetches the live document even when the cached copy is fresh.

maxage

Numeric scalar, the seconds a cached copy is used without asking the site; default 86400 (one day); Inf keeps a cached copy forever.

tmout

Numeric scalar, the seconds allowed for each of the two fetches (document and signature); default 20.

offline

Logical scalar, default FALSE: TRUE never fetches: the session's copy, the cached copy, then the bundled one (what the examples and an offline session get).

Value

A list with version (integer, 1), issued (the signing time, ISO 8601 UTC), notice (text for the user, possibly empty), llm (mode, base_url, auth_url: where the sign-in for the data key is reached; also models, default_model and request_access) and data (mode, base_url, license, request_access, and auth_url when the document has one), with the attribute "source" set to "live", "cache", "bundled" or "off".

Details

Every other MORIE package reads the same document through this function, so one sign-in and one document serve rmorie, rmoriedata and morie alike. Language models are never hosted: you bring your own key or model (llmask). The llm block of documents signed before that change carries the sign-in address only.

The environment variable MORIE_SERVICES_URL points the fetch at a mirror of the document (its signature is fetched from the same place, with the suffix .sig); the signature check is unchanged, so a mirror can only serve a document the project signed.

The order of resolution: a cached copy younger than maxage (unless refresh); the live document, fetched through the package's own checked transport (public https only, at most 1 MiB), verified, and kept only when it is not older than the copy already held or the bundled copy (an older signed document is a rollback and is refused); the stale cached copy; the bundled copy; and finally a document with every mode "off". A cached copy no newer than the bundled one is not used, and one that is older is deleted. Network failures are not errors: they fall through to the next copy.

Side effects: an accepted live document and its signature are written as morie-services.json and morie-services.sig to the folder tools::R_user_dir("rmoriebricklayer", "cache"). The result is also kept for the session, so later offline = TRUE calls (which the rest of the package makes) return it without checking the signature again.

Errors: refresh or offline not TRUE or FALSE; maxage not a single non-negative number; tmout not a single finite number of at least 1.

See also

dlogin, dmnf.

Examples

# Nothing is fetched here: the cached copy if there is one, else the
# document bundled with the package.
s <- svcs(offline = TRUE)
s$llm$mode
#> [1] "off"
attr(s, "source")
#> [1] "bundled"

# where the curated-data service is, and whether it takes a key
s$data[c("mode", "base_url")]
#> $mode
#> [1] "key"
#> 
#> $base_url
#> [1] "https://data.rmorie.com"
#> 
s$issued
#> [1] "2026-10-14T00:46:57Z"

# arguments are checked
try(svcs(maxage = -1))
#> Error : `maxage` must be a single non-negative number of seconds (Inf keeps a cached copy forever)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# ask the site now (network), and keep the answer for a day
svcs(refresh = TRUE)
} # }
